title: Introduction to API Routes
description: Write server‑side code right inside your Next.js app. Create your first endpoint in pages/api.

slides.title: The Serverless Backend ☁️
slides.content:
# What are API Routes?

Next.js lets you create API endpoints **without a separate server**.

Any file inside `pages/api/` is treated as an API endpoint instead of a React page.

* `pages/api/hello.js` → `/api/hello`
* Runs on the server (Node.js).
* You can access databases, APIs, secrets — anything you'd do in a backend.

It's like having a mini Express.js app baked in!

slides.title: Your First API Route (pages/api/hello.js)
slides.content: Export a default function that receives `req` and `res`.

quizData.question: Where do you create API routes?
quizData.explanation: The `pages/api` directory is special. Any file inside automatically becomes an API endpoint.

slides.title: Request & Response Objects 📨
slides.content:
# `req` and `res`

* **`req`**: An instance of `http.IncomingMessage`, plus some helpers.
  * `req.method` – GET, POST, etc.
  * `req.query` – the query string parameters.
  * `req.body` – the parsed request body (only after you parse it).
* **`res`**: An instance of `http.ServerResponse`, plus helpers.
  * `res.status(code)` – set HTTP status.
  * `res.json(data)` – send JSON response.
  * `res.send()` – send plain text.

No need for Express – but the pattern feels very similar.

slides.title: Handling Different Methods (pages/api/echo.js)
slides.content: Use `req.method` to determine the HTTP verb.
